significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a "prediction [that] becomes correct and stable" in the residual stream predicts the eventual answer early enough that terminating the remaining CoT preserves accuracy, with commitment tending to occur earlier on easier items; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling and ordering, not merely an existence claim. It establishes a behavioral phenomenon and an operational internal marker, but not a full causal mechanism for reasoning: it fixes when later tokens can be treated as redundant and informs adaptive-compute decisions of the kind motivated by Schuster et al.'s CALM, while linear decodability alone does not show where the answer was computed. A negative result would meaningfully rule out stable linear answer commitment as a general basis for early exit, although it would not rule out nonlinear or otherwise inaccessible commitment, so the negative branch is informative but bounded. After substituting away the specific stable-readout/future-answer coupling, the broad topic of mechanistic efficient reasoning would not merit this score; the coupling, early-exit consequence, and commitment-verbalization gap are the claim-specific increment over the topic-median confidence probe.

reach.justification: The named handle is a "cheap probe" combined with the rule to "declare commitment when the predicted answer is unchanged for W consecutive checks," yielding a concrete online early-exit controller rather than only an explanatory description. It is ex ante: the signal fires before the remaining reasoning tokens are generated and leaves an immediate action window to stop generation and reduce latency or cost. Although the probe may require per-model recalibration, the asserted predictive relation survives re-extraction—the claim predicts that stable commitment will precede verbalization and identify safe exits—rather than merely providing an unconstrained procedure for looking. The hypothesis spans open-weight reasoning models and math and logic tasks, and its downstream users include inference-system practitioners who gate or ship model outputs; deleting this particular controller and predictive coupling leaves only the topic and would not justify the same reach score.
